_comment: Canonical structured record of every revenue lane researched. The Obsidian vault under 'PERPETUA ORBITAL/' is GENERATED from this file by `node ops.mjs vault` — edit here, never edit the notes directly, or the next regeneration overwrites them. LANES.md keeps the narrative reasoning; this keeps the facts.

_verdicts.flagged: possible but with a serious caveat
_verdicts.unresearched: no findings — absence of data, not a negative

_policyValues.note: none-found means NO RULE WAS LOCATED. That is a gap and unallocated risk, never permission.

generatedNote: Dates are when the policy page itself was last verified, not when we read about it second-hand. Round 3 (2026-07-28, deep-research, 106 agents): Apify Store added as candidate; PromptBase and GPT Store resolved to flagged; itch.io and D2D disqualified. Partial primary-source data exists for Unity Asset Store (AI allowed with disclosure in submission guidelines; automation unknown), Fab/Unreal (EULA fetched, unverified), Cults3D (20% commission, EUR 5 floor, 15-day payout cycle; AI/automation language unknown), MyMiniFactory, Pond5 — none verified end-to-end, so they stay unresearched rather than cleared. Also still open: Hugging Face paid Spaces, MCP registries, Printables, Thangs, Artlist, RapidAPI.

lanes.name: Etsy
lanes.economics: 6.5% transaction + 3% + $0.25 processing + $0.20/listing
lanes.summary: Lane 1. Etsy's 2025 Creativity Standards explicitly accommodate AI goods with 'Designed by' attribution plus disclosure. All five product types verified against the live Printify catalog, all US-fulfilled, all clearing the $5 margin floor on measured costs.
risks: Production partner must be declared in Etsy BEFORE publishing or listings read 'Made by seller' — a leading POD suspension trigger
New-shop payment reserve delays cash

lanes.name: eBay
lanes.economics: 13.6% FVF + $0.30/$0.40; 250 free listings/mo then $0.35; Basic Store $27.95/mo
lanes.timeToCash: ~2 days after delivery with tracking; 31 days without
lanes.summary: Best-founded alternative marketplace. The User Agreement (effective 2026-06-28) binds you to responsibility for 'listing content created using tools offered by eBay or third parties such as translation, image editing, and generative artificial intelligence tools' — contract-level acknowledgment rather than silence. Its automation ban carries 'except with the prior express permission of eBay', and the Developers Program is that permission. Dropshipping from a wholesale supplier is expressly allowed, so Printify fulfilment is compliant.
risks: AI clause covers listing CONTENT, not explicitly product DESIGNS
eBay publishes no new-seller limit number; the ubiquitous '10 items/$500' is vendor-blog only
'A large increase in order volume' is a listed payment-hold trigger — ramp deliberately
corrections: The widely-reported 21-day new-seller hold is REFUTED — zero occurrences of '21 day' on the live holds page

lanes.name: Creative Market
lanes.economics: 50% to seller by default
lanes.summary: Best fit for the existing asset pipeline — the only top-ranked digital lane that consumes what we already produce at zero marginal cost. AI position is a documented yes (a labelling system announced 2025-05-02) rather than the silence others offer. Silence can be reinterpreted overnight; a published labelling regime cannot.
risks: A May 2025 policy 'to elevate unique work and discourage repetitive submissions' is aimed squarely at batch-generated variants — the single most likely thing to end this lane
Buyer-facing AI filters are planned, which will throttle demand on labelled listings
corrections: Commission is NOT unpublished — 50% default, in the help centre. The conflicting 40%/30% figures trace to a blog about Creative Market's own cut changing years ago
lanes.killCriteria: Stop if the shop application is rejected, or if listings get flagged under the repetitive-submissions policy.

lanes.name: Vecteezy
lanes.economics: not recorded
lanes.timeToCash: 6-12 weeks: ~21-day review, then a sale, then $25 payout floor
lanes.summary: The ONLY platform across both research rounds whose binding contract authorises BOTH AI content and automated publishing. Contributor Agreement s3(e) permits uploading 'using internal Vecteezy tools or other tools approved by Vecteezy (e.g., FTP)', names approved third-party uploaders, and its AI policy accepts AI-rendered images with no release required for text-prompt-only work. Everywhere else the best case was an unwritten gap — and a written yes is not the same asset.
risks: The binding constraint is the weekly Submission Quota, which tightens on low approval rate, where REJECTED FILES STILL CONSUME QUOTA and technically-rejected files can never be resubmitted. A high-volume low-quality pipeline throttles itself into a corner
The lane itself is shrinking — Shutterstock's content revenue went $789M (2022) to $760M (2024) while its AI training-data line grew 4.5x to $175M
lanes.killCriteria: Treat as a cheap bounded experiment, not a business line. Quality gate before upload is the whole game.

lanes.name: Gumroad
lanes.summary: Inverts the Redbubble pattern — actively built FOR agent automation. The official CLI README reads 'Designed for humans and AI agents alike', it documents GUMROAD_ACCESS_TOKEN for CI and agents, exposes POST /v2/products for programmatic creation, carries an ai_product_details_generations endpoint, and explicitly permits multiple accounts. True worldwide merchant of record, so it carries the EU/UK VAT liability.
risks: The advertised '10% + $0.50' EXCLUDES card processing — its own help article says so. Real cost roughly doubles at low price points
$100 payout minimum means ~50 sales at $10 before you see money
Bans reselling PLR/MRR outright, naming our exact categories: ebooks, courses, prompts, notion planners, templates, fonts, presets
corrections: The $100 threshold claim was TRUE — pinned to a commit in Gumroad's own open-source repo dated 2026-03-23, corroborated by Wayback snapshots either side

lanes.name: Framer
lanes.economics: 100% revenue share — 'Framer takes a 0% cut' — plus 50% of referred subscriptions
lanes.summary: Best raw terms found anywhere: 100% revenue share, no manual review gate, and an article dated 2026-07-24 actively urging creators to build 'AI-ready templates'. It should rank first and does not.
risks: Framer is a GUI canvas app with NO authoring API. Agents can do research, copy, imagery, SEO and the listing; a human must assemble the canvas. Realistic automation 60-80%, not 90-95%
No review gate means no scarcity — 2,000+ templates and creators publicly unhappy about the flood

UNRESOLVED CONFLICT: one agent quotes Community Terms s6.3 saying Framer 'does not process, collect, hold, or disburse any payments'; another describes a $200 minimum monthly payout. Read the terms directly before planning around either

lanes.name: Webflow
lanes.economics: 95% to creator since Oct 2025 (not the widely-quoted 80%)
lanes.timeToCash: paid ~15th of the following month, so 15-45 days
lanes.summary: Submissions are open — a previously assumed closure is out of date. Best demand data of any digital lane, from a named creator with 16 published templates: year 1 ~$4,800 on 11 templates, year 2 (7 months) ~$10,750 on 5. Roughly $29-64 per sale, ~25 lifetime sales per template.
risks: Requires THREE sites you have already built in Webflow before you may apply — a chicken-and-egg cost before dollar one
~7,000 templates against ~300 approved creators, with an explicitly tightening bar
Review screens for 'visual flair, polished typography, interactions' — the exact profile an AI-volume strategy fails

lanes.name: Whop
lanes.economics: 0% marketplace fee + 2.7% + $0.30
lanes.summary: The only course/community platform with a real discovery surface and zero fixed cost. Podia, Teachable and Kajabi have no marketplace at all — their /discover and /marketplace URLs 404 — so paying Kajabi $179/mo with no audience is buying a shop on a road with no cars.
risks: Marketplace service fee is NOT published anywhere — the widely-cited 3% is unverified, so margins cannot be modelled
July 2026 seller terms added mandatory KYC, a <1% dispute requirement, 180-day reserves, and power to claw back withdrawals from your bank account
Merchant of record for card settlement ONLY; its binding seller terms cover just 18 US states for tax while its help centre implies all 50
corrections: The '3% marketplace fee' is FALSE — it went to 0% per Whop's own changelog (2025-05-12)
The '$8,413 average creator earnings' figure appears on NO Whop-owned page; independent estimates put 87.8% of Whop products at $0/mo, median $74/mo

lanes.name: Amazon Merch on Demand
lanes.economics: royalty-based; a June 2026 restructure reportedly halves royalties without external traffic
lanes.summary: $0 cost and enormous traffic, but three problems. Amazon's public content guidelines contain no mention of AI at all, and Amazon itself launched an AI prompt-to-merch generator in June 2026 — so it will not ban AI designs. That same launch is the threat: the platform now competes directly with the product.
risks: Application is a lottery — 2 weeks to 3 months, no communication, approval not guaranteed
A June 2026 royalty restructure is reported by four independent tool vendors to cut royalties ~50% for sellers with no external traffic. UNVERIFIED against Amazon, whose policy pages are auth-gated
Starts at 10 upload slots
corrections: Printify's Amazon channel is NOT Merch on Demand — it is Seller Central, requiring a $39.99/mo Professional plan plus a GTIN exemption per category

lanes.name: Spoonflower
lanes.economics: 10% royalty scaling to 15% by volume tier
lanes.timeToCash: every 14 days, $10 minimum — the fastest verified anywhere
lanes.summary: Seller Agreement (effective 2025-12-19) contains zero mentions of AI, automation, bots or scraping. Its automation clause is read-side only ('not to crawl, scrape, or spider'), so automated uploading is unprohibited.
risks: As of 2026-05-28 there is an Artist Application: 5 distinct sample designs, tax documents, human review — and 'you may not re-apply if your application is denied'. One shot, human-juried, PERMANENT denial. A non-recoverable risk for an AI-design pipeline
corrections: The prior 403 was a bot-block, not a dead page — curl with a browser user-agent returned HTTP 200
Weekly listing limit is 50/artist/week, not the 25 that search snippets claimed

lanes.name: Displate
lanes.economics: flat royalties $4.50 / $9.00 / $14.50 by size
lanes.summary: The live FAQ states Verified Creator status covers work 'whether created entirely by hand or with assistance from the latest technologies like AI'.
risks: No upload API, and SMS identity verification is required before first publication — blocks headless automation in practice
The clause that actually bites is anti-duplication: re-uploading with 'only minor changes to the color palette, composition' is prohibited, and zero-sale designs are removed after 3 months
corrections: The widely-repeated Displate AI ban is REFUTED — every source asserting it is an SEO content farm; no primary document supports it

lanes.name: TikTok Shop
lanes.economics: all-in cost of sale 35-55% once fees, affiliate commission, shipping and returns are counted
lanes.timeToCash: mandatory 31-day introductory settlement period, then ~15 days
lanes.summary: Clearest AI policy of any lane — AI product imagery allowed with a visible 'AI-generated' label. Native Printify integration, US sellers only.
risks: No meaningful organic product search — sales come from video, which we do not produce
35-55% all-in cost of sale is near-zero on POD margins
TikTok banned AI voices in live commerce streams (July 2026), so the direction of travel is AI assets fine, AI presence not

lanes.name: Udemy
lanes.economics: 15% subscription / 37% organic / 97% self-referred
lanes.summary: Permissive on tooling — AI voice and AI video explicitly accepted — and restrictive on exactly what makes this model work.
risks: 'Udemy does not accept courses that are entirely AI-generated'
'Using AI to rapidly generate multiple low-quality courses... may even lead to removal from the platform' — the volume strategy is named almost verbatim as removal-worthy
The only good rate (97%) requires you to bring the traffic, in which case Udemy is just a cheap checkout

lanes.name: Amazon Associates
lanes.economics: 1-10% by category, 24-hour cookie
lanes.summary: No AI-content clause exists — verified by grepping the 77KB Operating Agreement and 133KB Policies for 'artificial', 'auto-generated' and 'machine learning'. Zero hits. That is a gap, not permission.
risks: 180 DAYS to refer a qualifying sale or the application is withdrawn, and Amazon 'is unable to reinstate' it
Automation clause is sharp: no 'artificially generate clicks or impressions... whether by way of a robot or software program'
24-hour cookie is punishing

lanes.name: Redbubble
lanes.economics: 50% platform fee on Standard tier, capped $150/period
lanes.summary: THE ANCHOR CASE for the automation lens. Redbubble publishes no AI-content policy at all — zero AI articles across 90 help-centre results — but its Community Guidelines make it an account-deletion trigger to upload 'using any bot, scraper, or other automated means for any purpose without our written permission'. That restricts automated UPLOADING, which is the operating model itself, not AI generation. Every guru post calling Redbubble AI-friendly misses it.
risks: Standard tier is explicitly defined by 'high volumes of low-effort designs, use of unmodified clip art, poor file quality, and tag spamming' and costs 50%
Hard ceiling of 30 uploads/day
lanes.reconsiderIf: Written permission for automated uploading is obtained — the terms explicitly contemplate it.

lanes.name: Envato
lanes.summary: Four independent blockers, any one fatal. New author accounts cannot be created. AI content is banned in the download file across ALL content types, not just audio. Revenue flattened to 50%. Envato states Elements 'continues to be our core focus'.
risks: 'Authors are not allowed to sell AI-generated content... This extends to all content types, across Market and Elements' — edited 2026-05-18, so it survived the Shutterstock acquisition
When intake reopens it explicitly EXCLUDES Theme, Code, Photo, Audio and Graphics

lanes.name: Skillshare
lanes.economics: royalty pool; 50-follower minimum since 2026-01-01
lanes.timeToCash: paid via Tipalti on the 16th, 16-45 day lag
lanes.summary: New teacher onboarding is PAUSED in Development, Home & Lifestyle, Writing & Publishing, Personal Development, Marketing & Business, Music & Audio, and Productivity — essentially every category an agent operation would target. The platform has publicly positioned against us: 'more of the internet is being optimized for scale, automation, and infinite content... Skillshare is making a deliberate choice to invest in being more human.'
risks: Skillshare's own published figure: 90% of the teachers cut by its new threshold earned under $5/month

lanes.name: Figma Community
lanes.economics: 15% Figma fee, creator keeps 85%
lanes.timeToCash: 30 US BUSINESS days after each sale — about 6 weeks
lanes.summary: 'We are not approving new creators to sell paid files on Community at this time.' Paid files — templates and UI kits, exactly the AI-automatable asset class — are closed to new sellers. Only paid plugins and widgets remain, which is engineering behind an approval with no published SLA.

lanes.name: Society6
lanes.economics: 5% markup on most products, 10% on prints — of BASE price, not retail
lanes.summary: Signup is closed — 'We're not accepting new applications right now' — following mass artist-account closures in two 2025 waves with 'no appeals process'. Worst economics reviewed. ToS bans 'any robot, spider, scraper, or other automated means... for any purpose', with frozen payments as the remedy.
corrections: The company is NOT shutting down — it appears as a going concern in Graham Holdings' Q1 2026 10-Q. Only the artist programme was gutted
risks: Society6 DELETED both artist-transition announcements from its live help centre; they survive only in the Internet Archive

lanes.name: Zazzle
lanes.economics: 5-50% self-set royalty, minus fees
lanes.timeToCash: $50 PayPal, up to 45 days after month end
lanes.summary: AI is allowed with a #generativecontent tag. Automation is the blocker: s3.1.16 bans automated retrieval 'including... AI, machine learning, and data science purposes', and the Creator FAQ is blunt — 'Automated scraping tools or bots are prohibited... may lead to Account termination or withheld Earnings.' Its API is a referral/preview toy, not an upload API.

lanes.name: Threadless
lanes.economics: ~10% on the Marketplace, which is juried
lanes.summary: Worst fit examined. Terms ban any automated system hitting the site 'more... than a human can reasonably produce'. Mandatory AI disclosure in every product description, plus an explicit right to 'remove designs that appear to be generated in bulk using artificial intelligence tools'.

lanes.name: Fine Art America
lanes.economics: 100% of your markup; free tier 25 images, $30/yr unlimited
lanes.summary: Easiest signup and best headline economics, undone by the broadest anti-bot clause reviewed: it covers 'any other automatic device, program, algorithm, or methodology' to ACCESS the site, plus an anti-deniability agency clause — 'Tools that use the Website shall be considered agents of the individuals who control or author them.'
risks: Terms are dated June 2020, PRE-generative-AI. The AI silence is an artifact of age and could close overnight

lanes.name: Temu
lanes.economics: commission UNPUBLISHED
lanes.summary: Genuinely surprising: automated uploading is expressly sanctioned via a public API, and signup is open to individuals with no LLC. POD fulfilment is what kills it.
risks: ~1 operating day handling time, $5/order late penalties, and you pay return shipping — incompatible with print-on-demand lead times
Temu WITHDREW its seller agreement from public access during 2025

lanes.name: Wayfair
lanes.economics: unpublished monthly Platform Access Fee; Net 60 with setoff rights
lanes.summary: Disqualifiers are model-level, not policy-level.
risks: Requires a warehouse or 3PL address and physical inventory
$1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate liability insurance
One-listing-per-product rule targets AI-variant economics directly
$75,000-per-file liquidated damages for competitive use of site materials — relevant if an agent scrapes it

lanes.name: Walmart Marketplace
lanes.economics: not recorded
lanes.summary: Requires US EIN, US business address, W-9, a product catalog and a US fulfilment address. Walmart explicitly prioritises sellers with established ecommerce track records. A solo POD seller with no marketplace history is a likely reject.

lanes.name: Alamy
lanes.economics: not recorded
lanes.summary: AI banned by an amendment dated 2026-07-13. The timing rule matters: existing contributors have until 1 September, but 'for Contributors who registered from 13 July 2026 onwards, the new contract was in force from the point of registration'. A new account today is bound immediately.
risks: Alamy's own public blog announcing the July changes lists commission and threshold changes and never mentions the AI ban

lanes.name: Shutterstock
lanes.economics: n/a
lanes.summary: 'Shutterstock does not accept AI-generated content from our contributors.' Note the ban lives in a help-centre article, not the contributor contract, which is dated 2023-09-05 and contains no AI or automation clause at all. Its AI contributor fund pays only for training-data licensing of already-uploaded back catalogues — with no back catalogue there is nothing to enter.
risks: The Shutterstock-Getty merger was TERMINATED 2026-07-07; Shutterstock's CEO stepped down five days later. Neither company has said anything to contributors

lanes.name: Getty / iStock
lanes.economics: n/a
lanes.summary: 'Will visuals I have generated or modified be offered as part of iStock's creative library? No.' Getty's contributor compensation for AI is training-data licensing on existing catalogues, with formula, eligibility and cadence published nowhere.

lanes.name: Lemon Squeezy
lanes.summary: Being sunset into Stripe. The CEO's post (2026-01-28) confirms the team has moved to Stripe Managed Payments; signup now routes into a triage that pitches Stripe's MoR products; no product updates since Aug 2025. Do not build here.

lanes.name: Shopify
lanes.summary: Worst of both worlds at this stage. Its own Terms state twice that 'the Services are not a marketplace' and 'You are the seller or merchant of record for all sales.' There is NO Shopify MoR path for a digital-only seller — Managed Markets prohibits digital goods and states a digital-only order makes you MoR automatically.
risks: Real cost is not $29/mo — it is $29/mo PLUS carrying EU/UK VAT registration personally from the first international sale
Zero attached buyer demand; a new domain starts at zero organic traffic
lanes.reconsiderIf: There is an audience or a proven paid-acquisition channel.

lanes.name: Display ad networks
lanes.economics: Ezoic 250,000 monthly active users; Raptive 25k pageviews + 6-month-old domain; Mediavine Official $5,000+ annual ad revenue
lanes.summary: Every floor moved up within twelve months, and Ezoic — the beginner on-ramp — now demands 250k monthly active users. Mediavine terminates for 'excessive use of Artificial Intelligence'; Raptive requires 'meaningful human involvement'. Combined with 68% of US Google searches ending without a click, the write-pages-and-monetise lane is structurally closed to a new domain.

lanes.name: B2B data / lead lists
lanes.economics: $6,000/yr California data-broker registration before dollar one
lanes.summary: Not a judgment call, a number. California's Delete Act sets 2026 annual data-broker registration at $6,000, due 31 January, with $200/day penalties for failing to register. That fixed compliance cost precedes the first dollar and kills the economics for a solo operator in California.

lanes.name: Etsy digital downloads
lanes.economics: $0.20/listing; no incremental shop cost inside Lane 1
lanes.timeToCash: 1-4 weeks to first sale per community reports
lanes.summary: Round 1's top queued lane. ~95% automatable, sells into the shop we are already opening, and reuses the fall/holiday design language at zero marginal design cost. The Halloween/fall SVG window opens around August — the one piece of timing here that actually expires.
risks: Template flips are banned; only original design qualifies
New-seller payment reserve can hold ~30% of funds for 45 days

lanes.name: Amazon KDP
lanes.economics: $0 to publish; 50% royalty on print books under $9.99 since June 2025, so price at $9.99+
lanes.timeToCash: royalties pay ~60 days after month end — day 75-90
lanes.summary: Round 1 lane #3. KDP accepts AI-generated content if disclosed via a mandatory private checkbox. Real consumer demand: 'coloring pages for adults' at 18,100/mo US.
risks: Enforcement targets undisclosed AI and low-quality mass uploads
Publishing capped at 3 titles/day
Cash lags badly — plan around 75-90 days

lanes.name: Notion templates
lanes.economics: Marketplace 10% + $0.40; Gumroad 10% + $0.50 + processing
lanes.timeToCash: Marketplace biweekly, $20 min, 14-day hold; Gumroad ~7 days
lanes.summary: Round 1 lane #4 and the most agent-native product on any list — templates are structured text, databases and formulas. Semrush shows 'notion templates' at 22,200/mo US.
risks: No policy against AI-built templates was found — permitted by silence, which is a gap
Marketplace requires waitlist plus approval; run Gumroad and the free gallery meanwhile

lanes.name: Fiverr productized gigs
lanes.economics: 20% commission, 14-day clearance
lanes.summary: Round 1 lane. Fiverr's Community Standards state AI is permitted across every category, and it has had dedicated AI categories since Jan 2023. Sells exactly what our agents already do for Lane 1 — Semrush-backed Etsy SEO audits, titles and tags, description packs. Doubles as paid market intelligence.
risks: Lowest automation of the round-1 set at ~85% — deliverables are fully agent-made but buyer messaging needs operator presence

lanes.name: Creative Fabrica
lanes.economics: 50% rev share on CF-referred, 75% self-referred; subscription downloads pay cents
lanes.summary: Round 1 lane #5. The most AI-forward marketplace found — it sells AI files natively. Pure syndication of the existing asset pipeline at roughly zero marginal cost.
risks: A trickle lane — seller reports around $1K in a first year
Subscription downloads pay cents
lanes.killCriteria: If under $50/mo after 90 days at 200+ assets, stop adding and let it idle.

lanes.name: FHT shop skills as a service
lanes.economics: $200-400/mo per shop (anchored on Podium ~$399/mo, Birdeye $299-449 — both third-party figures)
lanes.timeToCash: immediate — direct invoice, no platform escrow
lanes.summary: The strongest lane found in round 2, and the product already exists. ~/FHT AUTO INC/ holds 20 production shop skills running live since June 2026, including a 27KB fht-mitchell-writeup encoding Mitchell 1 line-type discipline and California BAR Write-It-Right constraints. Domain credibility in a trade is the one input that has not been commoditised — anyone can generate a website; almost nobody selling AI to repair shops has written a repair order that printed on BAR paperwork. Market is ~273,000 US independent shops.
risks: For the first 3-5 customers this is a JOB, not a system — you personally on the phone, you personally doing each shop-facts interview
It only becomes a system if the same shop-facts template works across shops without you. Test that assumption early and cheaply
Shops are famously cheap on software; distribution is genuinely hard
lanes.killCriteria: Free two-week pilot with five non-competing shops. The whole test is one question: do they paste the output unedited, or rewrite it? If they rewrite it, the domain encoding did not transfer.

lanes.name: White-label agency subcontracting
lanes.economics: wholesale $350-8,000/mo, resale 2-2.5x (LOW confidence — all sources are white-label vendors selling the model)
lanes.summary: Highest automation ratio of any services lane at ~90-95%, for one structural reason: the agency owns the client relationship. Client communication is the automation ceiling everywhere else; here it is someone else's problem. You get a spec, you return a deliverable.
risks: Concentration — one agency is one client who can drop you, and will squeeze margin once they see the output is AI
You are the commodity

lanes.name: PromptBase
lanes.economics: 20% marketplace fee; 0% via own referral link (30-day window); 10% custom jobs; Stripe or Zoneless payouts, configurable daily/weekly/monthly
lanes.timeToCash: payout floor exists but its amount is unpublished; formal ToS page 404s
lanes.summary: Fee structure triple-verified on live primary pages. The blocker is contractual: the T&Cs strictly prohibit "any automated tools, including but not limited to web crawlers, scrapers, or bots, to access ... any portion of our marketplace" — which forecloses the autonomous lane. Manual selling remains possible but earnings evidence is thin: one documented seller made $6 in month one, $28 in month two.
risks: Automation ban is blanket bot language — an agent-run listing pipeline would breach it on day one
Only third-party earnings datapoint found: $6 then $28/month (Medium, Jun 2024)
Older payout blog is stale — its $30 floor and fixed schedules were refuted against the live support page

lanes.name: Hugging Face / GPT Store / MCP registries
lanes.economics: GPT Store: NO platform revenue share for an individual US dev in 2026 — "Plugin developers are responsible for choosing how to monetize"; external merchant checkout only; embedded checkout is a partner-gated beta
lanes.timeToCash: n/a — no direct payout channel exists
lanes.summary: GPT Store half resolved with high confidence: OpenAI pays individual developers nothing platform-side in 2026; the Jan-2024 engagement-pay pilot was invite-only and never opened. The Hugging Face paid Spaces and MCP-registry halves produced no surviving claims and remain genuinely unresearched.
risks: Monetizing a GPT means running your own checkout site — that is a storefront lane, not a marketplace lane
HF paid Spaces / MCP registries: still no data — unresearched, not cleared

lanes.name: Apify Store
lanes.economics: 80% revenue share on Rental / Pay-per-Result / Pay-per-Event; PPE lets the Actor charge programmatically from its own source code; $20 PayPal payout floor ($100 other), monthly invoice cycle
lanes.timeToCash: monthly invoices, 3-day deemed-approval; sub-floor balances roll over, forfeited after 12 months below floor
lanes.summary: The strongest agent-operable lane round 3 found — the only platform whose LEGAL TERMS contain programmatic monetization: Store Publishing Terms (Feb 2026) grant 80% of user fees and PPE "allows you to programmatically charge for events in your Actor source code." Agentic payments (x402/Skyfire) let AI agents discover, run and pay for Actors with no Apify account; eligibility is automatic for PPE Actors. Apify reports ~$1.4M/month paid to third-party developers. Different business than design: the product is working software (scrapers, automations), which the operator side of this project already produces.
risks: The $1.4M/month and "many earn $3k" figures are unaudited first-party marketing; a testimonial on the same page took 15 months to first profit
Agentic-payments feature is ~1 month old and its rules are visibly shifting — re-verify before building
Open question: whether the PUBLISHER side (create/price/publish an Actor) is fully API-drivable or gated by KYC/manual review

lanes.name: itch.io
lanes.economics: open revenue share (creator sets it); butler CLI is first-party for BUILD uploads
lanes.summary: Three strikes in the quality guidelines, all verified verbatim: AI content must be tagged (delisting for failure), "do not use automated systems to mass produce product pages", and projects "predominantly created by algorithms or AI with minimal human intervention" are a restricted category regardless of disclosure. The butler CLI sanctions uploading builds to existing pages only — page creation has no public API. The exact combination we need is the exact combination they prohibit.
risks: Do not re-research: the mass-production ban plus the predominantly-AI restriction forecloses the autonomous pipeline by design

lanes.name: Draft2Digital / Kobo
lanes.economics: D2D: 15% of net receipts; royalties ~15 business days after month close
lanes.summary: D2D content guidelines: "we do not accept content that has been generated entirely by AI/LLMs that has not gone through extensive editing from a human", plus a ban on mass-produced content. An autonomous ebook pipeline is precisely what that excludes. (Claims fetched from primary pages but not triple-verified — the verdict rests on the quoted guideline language.)
risks: KDP (already a candidate lane) remains the better ebook route — its bar is disclosure, not mandatory human editing
